change_summary: The PLOS One Editors have retracted the article Detecting phishing websites using machine learning technique, because it was one of a series of submissions with concerns about peer review integrity and potential manipulation of the publication process. The editors say these concerns call into question the validity and provenance of the reported results, which include the proposed LSTM-based detector's accuracy of 97.4% on Phishtank and 96.8% on Crawler data. The author either did not respond to the editors or could not be reached.
evaluation: In Section 3, your draft names Dutta [14] as the main evidence for its choice of detector, an RNN-LSTM URL detector called LURL, and cites [14] for LURL's accuracy of 97.4% on Phishtank and 96.8% on Crawler data, higher than both comparison detectors; the stored paper reports those accuracies. On the strength of these results the draft chose an LSTM over the two alternatives it had first considered, and it decided not to run a separate model-selection study before the pilot. In Section 4, the draft starts from the LURL settings reported by Dutta [14]: two LSTM layers, hidden size 650, learning rate 1.0 with decay 0.73, and it does not plan to tune these settings before the pilot, so that its results can be read against the published ones. The PLOS One Editors have retracted the article because it was one of a series of submissions with concerns about peer review integrity and potential manipulation of the publication process. The editors say these concerns call into question the validity and provenance of the reported results, and those are the accuracy results your Section 3 relies on and the published results your Section 4 settings are meant to be read against, so all three uses are touched and the effect on your draft is high.
recommendation: The PLOS One Editors have retracted the article because it was one of a series of submissions with concerns about peer review integrity and potential manipulation of the publication process, and the editors say these concerns call into question the validity and provenance of the reported results. In Section 3, the draft names Dutta [14] as the main evidence for its choice of detector, and it cites [14] for LURL's accuracy of 97.4% on Phishtank and 96.8% on Crawler data, higher than both comparison detectors; on that basis, the draft decided not to run a separate model-selection study before the pilot. Remove or replace that citation, and re-check the LSTM choice with other evidence or the model-selection study you skipped. In Section 4, the draft starts from the LURL settings reported by Dutta [14] and does not plan to tune these settings before the pilot, so that its results can be read against the published ones. Raise this with your co-authors or supervisor before the pilot, because editing the text won't fix the planned method.
